entries.what_happened: Four manuscripts; none states the bullet verbatim. (1) “Numerical Semiampleness of Nef Adjoint Divisors” (Oct 3 2026, build/main.tex, introduction Theorem thm:main): for a projective klt Q-pair (X,B) over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, with K_X+B pseudo-effective, M a nef Q-Cartier divisor on X and K_X+B+M nef, the divisor K_X+B+M is numerically equivalent to a semiample Q-Cartier divisor. With B=0 and M=0 this is the bullet’s case (K_X nef). The introduction then cites Fukuda’s theorem to say a semiample numerical representative makes K_X+B itself semiample, so for M=0 the manuscript claims K_X is semiample, conditionally on its log abundance input (see conditional_on). (2) “Numerical semiampleness of nef adjoint classes on compact Kähler manifolds” (Oct 6 2026, build/main.tex): for smooth connected compact Kähler X, a rational snc boundary B with coefficients below one, and a rational nef M, if K_X+B is pseudo-effective and K_X+B+M is nef, then c_1(K_X+B+M) equals, in real Bott–Chern cohomology, the first Chern class of a semiample rational line bundle. With B=0, M=0 this covers smooth projective varieties with nef K_X, but only numerically: the paper says it “does not assert semiampleness of the original adjoint”. Singular klt varieties are outside its scope. (3) “Minimal models and Mori fibre spaces for generalized log canonical Q-pairs” (Sept 24 2026, build/main.tex): for projective generalized lc Q-pairs over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, a birational map to a model Y that extracts no divisors and does not lower discrepancies, with K_Y+B_Y+M_Y nef when the adjoint is pseudo-effective, and a Mori fibre space otherwise. The Corollary with M=0 gives the ordinary lc case. Semiampleness is not in its theorem; the paper says the companion log abundance theorem [OpenAILogAbundance2026, Thm 1.1] makes K_Y+B_Y semiample on that model Y, not on X. (4) “Minimal models in numerical dimension one” (Sept 24 2026, build/paper.tex): for a smooth connected complex projective X of dimension n at least 3 with K_X pseudo-effective and Nakayama’s section-growth invariant κ_σ(X,K_X)=1 (fixed ample twist), a finite sequence of K-negative divisorial contractions and flips X ⇢ Y to a Q-factorial terminal Y with K_Y nef, with p*K_X = q*K_Y + E, E effective. A Corollary makes Y a good minimal model via the same companion log abundance theorem. It says nothing about semiampleness of K_X on X itself.
entries.delivers: Unconditionally, none of the four manuscripts establishes semiampleness of K_X on a projective klt variety X. The Oct 3 manuscript, if its inputs are granted, claims the bullet’s B=0, M=0 case in every dimension, including the smooth case, over algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero; its stated theorem is numerical, and semiampleness of K_X is obtained only by citing Fukuda’s theorem. Its abstract calls the result the Generalised Abundance Conjecture of Lazić–Peternell, which is the M nonzero generalization of the bullet. The bullet names no field; the live article says a field k, and the manuscripts do not cover arbitrary fields of characteristic zero or characteristic p. The Kähler manuscript delivers only the numerical Bott–Chern statement for smooth compact Kähler manifolds, and for the projective case it says “Projective manifolds are covered by [P]”. The lc minimal-model and numerical-dimension-one manuscripts deliver nef minimal models on birational models; their semiampleness claims are for Y, and only through the companion log abundance theorem.
entries.remains: If the claims are correct: (a) fields other than algebraically closed fields of characteristic zero are not covered by any of the four; (b) for the lc minimal-model and numerical-dimension-one manuscripts, semiampleness of K_X on X itself is not addressed; (c) for the Kähler manuscript, singular klt varieties are not covered, and semiampleness rather than numerical semiampleness of K_X is not established; (d) for the numerical-dimension-one manuscript, every case with κ_σ different from 1, and dimensions below 3, remain; (e) for the Oct 3 manuscript, nothing remains on the bullet’s klt, B=0, M=0 case beyond the numerical-to-semiample step, which depends on Fukuda’s theorem as cited.
entries.direction: proves the conjecture conditionally (Oct 3, on a log abundance input); numerical or partial-case results elsewhere
entries.conditional_on: Oct 3 manuscript: (i) its Theorem input:abundance is log abundance for projective lc Q-pairs over an algebraically closed field of characteristic zero, cited as [LA] = OpenAI “Log abundance in characteristic zero”, Theorem 1.1; I did not read that paper. This statement contains the bullet’s klt, B=0 case, so the manuscript assumes it rather than proving it. (ii) The moving-jet and Frobenius results of [LA] (its Sections 7–9, Lemmas 7.1–7.5, Proposition 6.11, Theorem 9.1), which the manuscript adapts for the full-nef-dimension step (Theorem thm:terminal-big). (iii) The terminating minimal model programme for generalized klt pairs from [MM], which is the Minimal-models manuscript in this family (Theorem 1.1 and Section 3.3). (iv) Fukuda’s theorem [Fukuda, Theorem 0.1], to pass from numerical to actual semiampleness when M=0. (v) Published inputs such as BCHM and Birkar–Zhang. Kähler manuscript: its ordinary divisorial decomposition (Theorem pre:ordinary) is [K, Theorem 2.13] with the logarithmic Iitaka hypothesis from [LI, Corollary 6.2]; its projective case is [P, Proposition 8.1] with [P, Theorem 2.3]; its algebraic-dimension-zero case uses [BBYv2, Corollary 1.4], [Ou], [COP] and several cited results (Campana, Ueno, Kebekus–Schnell). lc minimal-model manuscript: semiampleness on Y depends on the companion [OpenAILogAbundance2026, Theorem 1.1]; the terminating transfer is credited to Tsakanikas–Xie, and the introduction says their programmes “have explicit existence or non-pseudo-effectivity hypotheses”. Numerical-dimension-one manuscript: the good-model Corollary depends on [OpenAILogAbundance2026, Theorem 1.1]; the main theorem uses BCHM Corollary 1.4.2 and standard MMP results, and in the parts I read it cites no other OpenAI manuscript.
entries.doubts: Oct 3: the text says its M=0 conclusion “is equivalent to ordinary klt abundance, which is an input to this proof”, and takes lc log abundance from [LA] as Theorem input:abundance. The abstract’s “We prove the Generalised Abundance Conjecture” therefore rests on that input. The main theorem is numerical (D ≡ L), and semiampleness of K_X for M=0 comes from citing Fukuda. The Frobenius comparison is said to “reproduce the comparison proof” of [LA] “with its uniformity conditions”. Kähler: the text says the statement does not assert semiampleness; the algebraic-dimension-zero case depends on Proposition zero:line-nonvanishing, which is stated under two line-subsheaf bounds that Lemma zero:cotangent-slope supplies, and the proof follows [K, Section 6] while giving its estimates. I did not check Sections 03, 04, 06 or most of 05. Minimal-models (lc): the text says the bounded-fibre theorem “only its reference form has bounded index”; the BFMT precedent is stated for klt singularities and the manuscript notes “the reference form here may be lc”; the transfer is credited to others. I read only Section 1 of twelve sections. Numerical-dimension-one: the finiteness of the canonical prefix comes from Lemma mmp:stabilization, a cycle-class dimension count adapted from [AHK07], a four-fold result; the introduction says the cycle arguments “do not assert termination of the concatenated programs”, so this step carries the finiteness claim in the theorem. Its semiampleness claim is conditional, as stated above.
